Surah Yunus (upon him be peace) is Meccan, except for three verses, from His saying: ﴿So if you are in doubt about what We have sent down to you﴾ to the end of them. In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.

* *

﴿Alif, Lam, Ra.﴾ And "Al-Mar" (ال مر). The people of the Hijaz, the people of Syria, and Hafs read the ra in both with a fatha (fath). The others read it with imala (imalah, the inclining of the vowel toward i). Ibn Abbas and al-Dahhak said: "Alif, Lam, Ra" means "Ana Allahu Ara" (I am Allah, the One who sees), and "Al-Mar" means "Ana Allahu A'lamu wa Ara" (I am Allah, the One who knows and sees).

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "Alif, Lam, Ra", "Ha, Mim", and "Nun" are letters of the name al-Rahman (the Most Merciful). The discussion of the disjointed letters (huruf al-tahajji) has already been covered [[Refer to what preceded: 1/58-59. And see all these opinions in: al-Tabari: 1/205-224.]].

﴿These are the verses of the Wise Book.﴾ That is, these; and by "the Wise Book" He means the Qur'an. It was also said: He meant by them the verses that He had sent down before that, and for this reason He said "these" (tilka), and "tilka" is a demonstrative for a feminine absent referent. "Al-Hakim" (the Wise) means the one made firm (al-muhkam) with regard to the lawful and the unlawful, the limits and the rulings; it is fa'il in the sense of maf'al, as evidenced by His saying: "A Book whose verses have been made firm" [Hud: 1].

It was also said: it means in the sense of al-hakim (the one who judges), fa'il in the sense of fa'il, its evidence being His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: "And He sent down with them the Book with the truth, that it might judge between the people" [al-Baqarah: 213].

It was also said: it means in the sense of al-mahkum (the one judged), fa'il in the sense of maf'ul. Al-Hasan said: it was judged within it with justice and excellence and giving to the kinsfolk, and with prohibition of immorality, wrongdoing and oppression; and within it was judged regarding Paradise for whoever obeys Him and the Fire for whoever disobeys Him.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 10, verses 2–3:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Is it a wonder for mankind?﴾ Al-'Ajab (wonder, astonishment): a state that overtakes a person upon seeing something contrary to the usual course of things.

The occasion of the revelation of the verse: When Allah, mighty and majestic, sent Muhammad (ﷺ) as a messenger, the polytheists said: "Allah is greater than that His messenger should be a human being." So He, exalted, said: ﴿Is it a wonder for mankind﴾ [[Narrated by al-Tabari from Ibn 'Abbas: 15/13. See also: Asbab al-Nuzul, p. 305; al-Durr al-Manthur: 4/340, where it is attributed to Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh, in a lengthy form.]] — meaning: the people of Makkah. **Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 10, verses 4–5:**

﴿To Him is your return, all of you. The promise of Allah is true.﴾ *Ṣidqan* (truly), with no doubt in it. It is in the accusative as a verbal noun (*maṣdar*, a verbal noun in the accusative), meaning: He promised you a true promise. ﴿Indeed, He originates creation, then repeats it.﴾ That is, He gives them life at the beginning, then causes them to die, then gives them life again. The reading of the majority is ﴿innahu﴾ with a *kasra* on the *alif*, as a new sentence (*istiʾnaf*, a resumed or independent clause). Abu Ja'far read *annahu* with a *fatḥa*, meaning "that He..." ﴿So that He may reward those who believed and did righteous deeds with justice﴾, that is, with fairness. ﴿As for those who disbelieved, they will have a drink of boiling water﴾, water whose heat has become extreme, ﴿and a painful punishment because they used to disbelieve.﴾

﴿It is He who made the sun a shining light﴾ by day, ﴿and the moon a light﴾ by night. It is also said: He made the sun possessed of brightness (*ḍiyāʾ*) and the moon possessed of light (*nūr*). ﴿And He determined for it stations﴾. That is, He determined for it, meaning He prepared for it stations which it does not exceed and does not fall short of. He did not say "He determined them" (in the dual).

It is said: the determination of the stations applies to both of them, but He suffices with mentioning only one of them, as He said: "Allah and His Messenger have more right that they should please Him" [al-Tawbah: 62].

It is also said: it refers to the moon specifically, because by the moon the ending of months and years is known, not by the sun.

The stations of the moon (*manāzil al-qamar*, the lunar mansions, the divisions of the sky through which the moon passes) are twenty-eight, and their names are: al-Sharṭayn, al-Buṭayn, al-Thurayyā, al-Dabarān, al-Haqʿah, al-Han'ah, al-Dhirāʿ, al-Nasr, al-Ṭawf, al-Jabhah, al-Zubrah, al-Ṣarfah, al-ʿAwwāʾ, al-Simāk, al-Ghafr, al-Zibānī, al-Iklīl, al-Qalb, al-Shawlah, al-Naʿāyim, al-Baldah, Saʿd al-Dhābiḥ, Saʿd Bulaʿ, Saʿd al-Suʿūd, Saʿd al-Akhbiyah, Farʿ al-Dalw al-Muqaddam, Farʿ al-Dalw al-Muʾakhkhar, and Baṭn al-Ḥūt.

These stations are divided among the constellations (*burūj*, the zodiacal signs), which are twelve: al-Ḥamal, al-Thawr, al-Jawzāʾ, al-Saraṭān, al-Asad, al-Sunbulah, al-Mīzān, al-ʿAqrab, al-Qaws, al-Jady, al-Dalw, and al-Ḥūt.

Each constellation contains two stations and a third of a station. The moon halts at one station each night, and it is hidden for two nights if the month is thirty days, or for one night if the month is twenty-nine days. Thus those stations are completed, and the sun's stay in each station is thirteen days, so the year ends when they end.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿That you may know the number of years﴾, that is, the measure of the stations, "that you may know the number of years" by their entering and their ending, ﴿and the reckoning﴾, meaning the reckoning of the months, days and hours.

﴿Allah did not create that﴾, He referred it to creation and determination. Had He referred it to the specific things mentioned, He would have said "those" (*tilka*).

﴿Except in truth﴾, that is, He did not create it in vain, but to manifest His craftsmanship and as evidence of His power.

﴿He details the signs for a people who know.﴾ Ibn Kathir, Abu ʿAmr, Ḥafṣ and Yaʿqūb read *yufaṣṣilu* with a *yāʾ*, referring to His saying "that He created." The rest read *nufaṣṣilu* with a *nūn*, as an expression of majesty.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 10, verses 6–9:

﴿Indeed, in the alternation of the night and the day, and in what Allah has created in the heavens and the earth, are signs for a people who fear Allah.﴾ "Who believe."

﴿Indeed, those who do not expect to meet Us﴾ means: they do not fear Our punishment and do not hope for Our reward. Al-rajaʾ (hope) can carry the meaning of fear and of desire. ﴿And they are content with the worldly life﴾ means they choose it and work for it. ﴿And they are at rest in it﴾ means they settle down in it.

﴿And those who are heedless of Our signs﴾ means: heedless of Our proofs, not taking heed. Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: "Our signs" refers to Muhammad (ﷺ) and the Qur'an. "Heedless" means turning away.

﴿Those, their refuge is the Fire because of what they used to earn﴾ from disbelief and denial.

His statement, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds, their Lord will guide them by their faith﴾ contains an idmar (an implied omission), meaning: their Lord will guide them by their faith to a Garden, ﴿beneath which rivers flow﴾. Mujahid said: He will guide them on the path (al-sirat) to the Garden, making for them a light by which they walk.

It is also said: the meaning of "yahdihim" is "yuthibuhum wa yajzihim" (He will reward them and recompense them).

It is also said: the meaning is that by their faith their Lord guides them to His religion; that is, by their affirmation He guided them. "Beneath which rivers flow" means "before them," as in His statement, Mighty and Majestic: "Your Lord has placed beneath you a stream" [Maryam: 24]. He did not mean that it was beneath her while she was sitting on it; rather He meant in front of her.

It is also said: "Beneath them rivers flow" means by their command. ﴿In gardens of bliss.﴾

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 10, verses 10–11:**

﴿Their call therein﴾ means their saying and their speech. It was also said: their supplication.

﴿Glory be to You, O Allah﴾ is a word of exaltation, by which Allah is declared free of every imperfection. We have also narrated: "The people of Paradise are inspired with praise and glorification, just as they are inspired with breath" [[From Jabir, who said: I heard the Prophet ﷺ say: "The people of Paradise eat and drink, but they do not spit, urinate, defecate, or blow their noses." They said: "Then what about the food?" He said: "Belching and perspiration like the perspiration of musk. They are inspired with glorification and praise as they are inspired with breath." Narrated by Muslim in the book on Paradise and its bliss, chapter on the attributes of Paradise and its people (3835): 4/2180–2181.]].

The people of tafsir (Qur'anic exegesis) said: this word is a sign between the people of Paradise and their servants regarding food. When they wish for food, they say, "Glory be to You, O Allah," and they are brought at once what they desire upon the tables. Each table is a mile by a mile, and upon each table are seventy thousand dishes, and in each dish is a kind of food unlike the others. When they finish eating, they praise Allah. This is the meaning of His words, Exalted is He: ﴿And the last of their call therein is: "All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds."﴾ [[As-Suyuti cited several reports on this. Ad-Durr al-Manthur: 4/345–346.]]

His words, Exalted is He: ﴿And their greeting therein is "Peace."﴾ That is, some of them greet one another with peace. It was also said: the greeting of the angels to them is peace.

It was also said: the angels come to them from their Lord with peace.

﴿And the last of their call is: "All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds."﴾ It means: they begin their speech with glorification and end it with praise.

His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿If Allah were to hasten for people the evil as they seek to hasten the good...﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: this refers to a man's saying in anger to his family and children, "May Allah curse you, and may He not bless you." Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 10, verse 12–13:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when harm touches man, he calls upon Us, lying on his side, or sitting or standing﴾ — "harm" (al-durr) means hardship and severity. ﴿He calls upon Us﴾ — that is, while lying on his side. ﴿Or sitting or standing﴾ — meaning in all his states, because a person cannot go beyond one of these states.

﴿But when We remove﴾ — i.e., We push away — ﴿from him his harm, he passes on as though he had never called upon Us against a harm that touched him.﴾ That is, he continues on his former course, before the harm reached him, and forgets the hardship and affliction he was in, as though he had never called upon Us against a harm that touched him, i.e., he did not ask Us to remove a harm that had touched him.

﴿Thus it is made fair-seeming to the transgressors﴾ — those who exceed the limit in disbelief and disobedience — ﴿what they used to do﴾ — of disobedience. Ibn Juraij said: "Thus it is made fair-seeming to the transgressors what they used to do" refers to their supplication in time of trial and their neglect of gratitude in time of ease. It was also said: its meaning is, just as your deeds were made fair-seeming to you, their deeds were made fair-seeming to the transgressors who were before you.

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿And We had already destroyed generations before you when they wronged﴾ — they associated partners with God — ﴿and their messengers came to them with clear proofs, but they were not going to believe. Thus﴾

That is: just as We destroyed them for their disbelief, ﴿We recompense﴾ — We punish and destroy — ﴿the criminal people﴾ — the disbelievers who denied Muhammad (ﷺ). He warns the disbelievers of Makkah with the punishment of the earlier nations who denied.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 10, verses 14–16:

﴿Then We made you successors (khala'if)﴾ i.e., successors (khulafa'), ﴿in the earth after them﴾ i.e., after the generations We destroyed, ﴿that We might see how you would act﴾, and He knows them best. We have related from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Indeed this world is sweet and green, and indeed Allah makes you successors in it, and He watches how you act" [[Narrated by Muslim in ar-Riqaq, chapter "Most of the People of Paradise are the Poor..." no. (2742): 4/2098, and the author in Sharh as-Sunnah: 9/12.]].

The saying of the Exalted and Majestic: ﴿And when Our clear verses are recited to them﴾. Qatadah [[In Asbab al-Nuzul of al-Wahidi p. 305: Mujahid. See also: ad-Durr al-Manthur: 4/347.]] said: they mean the polytheists of Makkah. Muqatil [[Asbab al-Nuzul p. 305.]] said: they were five men: Abdullah ibn Umayyah al-Makhzumi, al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah, Mikraz ibn Hafs, Amr ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Qays al-Amiri, and al-As ibn Amir ibn Hashim.

﴿Those who do not expect to meet Us say﴾, they are the ones previously mentioned, who said to the Prophet (ﷺ): If you want us to believe in you, ﴿bring a Qur'an other than this﴾, one in which there is no abandoning of the worship of al-Lat, al-Uzza and Manat, and no criticism of them. And if Allah has not revealed it, then say it yourself from your own self. ﴿Or change it﴾, so put a verse of punishment in place of a verse of mercy, or in place of a prohibited thing make a permitted thing, or in place of a permitted thing make a prohibited thing. ﴿Say﴾ to them, O Muhammad, ﴿It is not for me to change it on my own accord﴾, from my own side, ﴿I follow only what is revealed to me﴾, i.e., I follow only what is revealed to me concerning what I command you and forbid you from. ﴿Indeed I fear, if I disobey my Lord, the punishment of a tremendous day﴾.

﴿Say: If Allah had willed, I would not have recited it to you﴾, meaning: if Allah had willed, He would not have sent down the Qur'an upon me.

﴿Nor would He have made you know of it﴾, i.e., nor would Allah have informed you of it. Al-Bazzi, from Ibn Kathir, read "wa-la-adrakum bihi" with the short vowel (qasr) on the affirmative pattern, meaning: nor would He have taught you of it apart from my reciting it to you. Ibn Abbas read "wa-la andhartukum bihi" from the warning (inzar).

﴿Indeed I have remained among you a lifetime﴾, a period, which is forty years, ﴿before it﴾, before the revelation of the Qur'an, and I did not bring you anything.

﴿Will you not then reason?﴾ that it is not from me. The Prophet (ﷺ) remained among them before the revelation for forty years, then Allah revealed to him, and he remained in Makkah after the revelation for thirteen years, then he migrated and remained in Madinah for ten years, and he passed away at the age of sixty-three.

It was related by Anas that he remained in Makkah after the revelation for ten years and in Madinah for ten years, and he passed away at the age of sixty. The first is more well-known and more apparent [[Narrated by Ibn Abi Shaybah in al-Musannaf 13/54, 14/291, Ibn Sa'd in at-Tabaqat: 2/308, and Abd al-Razzaq: 3/599. See also: ad-Durr al-Manthur: 4/348-349, Kanz al-Ummal: no. (4750).]].

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 10, verse 17–19:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Who is more unjust than one who fabricates a lie against Allah?﴾ So he claims that He has a partner or a son. ﴿Or denies His signs?﴾ That is, Muhammad (ﷺ) and the Qur'an. ﴿Indeed, the criminals will not succeed﴾ — the polytheists will not be saved.

﴿And they worship other than Allah that which neither harms them﴾ if they disobey Him and abandon His worship, ﴿nor benefits them﴾ if they worship Him. He means the idols. ﴿And they say, "These are our intercessors with Allah." Say, "Do you inform Allah of that which He does not know﴾ — do you inform Allah, ﴿of that which He does not know﴾ of its truth? The meaning of the verse: Do you inform Allah that He has a partner, or that He has an intercessor with Him without His permission, while Allah does not know of any partner for Himself?! ﴿In the heavens or on the earth. Exalted is He above what they associate with Him.﴾ Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read "tushrikun" (you associate) with the ta' here, and in two places in Surah al-Nahl, and in Surah al-Rum; the others read all of them with the ya' (yushrikun).

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And mankind was not but one community﴾ — that is, upon Islam. We have mentioned the disagreement concerning it in Surah al-Baqarah [[See above: 1/243-244.]]. ﴿But they differed﴾ and became divided into believer and disbeliever. ﴿And if not for a word that preceded from your Lord﴾ — by which He appointed for every community a term. Al-Kalbi said: it is the respite granted to this community, and that He would not destroy them with punishment in this world. ﴿The matter would have been decided between them﴾ by the descent of punishment and the hastening of retribution upon the deniers, and that would have been a judgment between them. ﴿Concerning that over which they differ.﴾ Al-Hasan said: "And if not for a word that preceded from your Lord," which had passed in His decree, that He would not judge between them in what they differed over with reward and punishment except on the Day of Resurrection, the matter would have been decided between them in this world, so He would have admitted the believer to Paradise and the disbeliever to Hellfire; but Allah's appointed term had preceded, so He made their appointment the Day of Resurrection.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 10, verse 26:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿For those who have done good is the best (husna) and more (ziyadah)﴾. That is, for those who did good deeds in this world is the best (al-husna), which is Paradise, and more (ziyadah), which is looking upon the Noble Face of Allah. This is the saying of a group of the Companions, among them Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, Hudhayfah, Abu Musa, and 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit, may Allah be pleased with them all, and it is the saying of al-Hasan, 'Ikrimah, 'Ata', Muqatil, al-Dahhak, and al-Suddi.

Abu Sa'id Ahmad ibn [Muhammad ibn] al-'Abbas al-Humaydi informed us, Abu 'Abd Allah Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Hafiz informed us, Abu al-'Abbas Muhammad ibn Ya'qub informed us by dictation, Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-San'ani narrated to us, al-Aswad ibn 'Amir narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us from Thabit (i.e., al-Bunani), from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, from Suhayb, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited this verse: ﴿For those who have done good is the best and more﴾, and said: "When the people of Paradise enter Paradise and the people of the Fire enter the Fire, a caller will call out: 'O people of Paradise, you have a promise with Allah which He wishes to fulfill for you.' They will say: 'What is this promise? Has He not made our scales heavy, whitened our faces, admitted us into Paradise, and saved us from the Fire?' Then the veil will be lifted, and they will look upon the Face of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Nothing that has been given to them will be more beloved to them than looking at Him." (ﷺ)

It is related from Ibn 'Abbas that the best (al-husna) is that a good deed is rewarded with its like, and the increase (al-ziyadah) is the multiplication by ten times its like up to seven hundred times. Mujahid said: The best (al-husna) is one good deed like one good deed, and the increase is forgiveness and good pleasure.

[Al-Tabari said, may Allah have mercy on him: "The most correct of the sayings on this matter is to say: Allah, blessed and exalted, promised those among His servants who do good, in return for their good, the best, that He would reward them for their obedience to Him with Paradise and that their faces would be whitened; and He promised them, along with the best, an increase over it. Among the increase over their admission to Paradise is that He honors them by looking at Him, that He gives them chambers of pearls, and that He increases them in forgiveness and good pleasure. All of that is among the increases of Allah's bounty to them beyond the best which Allah has prepared for the people of His Gardens. Our Lord, may His praise be great, generalized by His saying 'and more' the increases over 'the best,' without specifying any of them over another. It is not disapproved of, from the bounty of Allah, that He should gather all of that for them; rather, all of it is gathered for them, if Allah wills. So the most correct of the sayings on this matter is that it be generalized, as He, may His remembrance be exalted, generalized it."]

﴿And darkness (qatar) will not cover their faces, nor humiliation (dhillah)﴾. Yarhaqu means: does not cover. Qatar means dust, the plural of qatrah. Ibn 'Abbas and Qatadah said: blackness of the face. Dhillah means disgrace. Qatadah said: sorrow. Ibn Abi Layla said: this is the extent of their looking at their Lord.

﴿Those are the companions of Paradise; therein they will abide forever﴾.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 10, verses 27–30:

﴿Those who have earned evil deeds—the recompense of an evil deed is its like﴾. That is: for them is its like, as He said: "And whoever comes with an evil deed, he will not be recompensed except with its like" [al-An'am: 160].

﴿And humiliation will cover them. They will have no protector from Allah﴾. The "min" (from) here is redundant (ṣilah), meaning: they have no protector from Allah. ﴿As if their faces had been covered﴾, that is, clothed, ﴿with pieces﴾ plural of qiṭʿah, ﴿of the night, dark﴾. It is in the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial qualifier) and not as a na't (adjective), and for this reason it does not say "muẓlimah" (feminine). Its sense is: pieces of the night in the state of its darkness, or pieces of the dark night. Ibn Kathir, al-Kisa'i and Ya'qub read "qiṭʿan" with the ṭāʾ sukun, meaning "some," as in His saying: "with a portion of the night" [Hud: 81].

﴿Those are the companions of the Fire; therein they will abide forever﴾.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And on the Day We gather them all, then We will say to those who associated partners: "Stay in your place, you and your partners"﴾ [that is: keep to your place] ﴿you and your partners﴾, meaning the idols. The meaning is: then We will say to those who associated partners: keep to your place, you and your partners, and do not depart.

﴿Then We will separate them﴾ we distinguish and divide, ﴿between them﴾, that is, between the polytheists and their partners, and We cut off what had been between them of connection in the world. This is when every object of worship besides Allah disowns those who worshipped it. ﴿And their partners will say﴾, meaning the idols: ﴿"You did not worship us"﴾ by our request. They will say: "Yes, we used to worship you." Then the idols will say:

﴿"Allah suffices as a witness between us and you; we were indeed unaware of your worship"﴾. That is: we were only unaware of your worship of us; we did not hear, did not see, and did not understand.

Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿There each soul will test﴾, that is, will be tested. It was said: its meaning is: it will know and become aware of it. Ḥamzah, al-Kisa'i and Ya'qub read "tatlū" with two tāʾs, meaning "will recite," ﴿every soul﴾ its record. It was said: its meaning is: every soul will follow ﴿what it sent forth﴾,

that is, what it had put forward of good or evil. It was said: its meaning is: it will witness it. ﴿And they will be returned to Allah﴾, to His judgment, so that He alone will judge them, ﴿their true Master﴾ who manages and possesses their affairs. If it is said: Did He not say: "And that the disbelievers have no protector" [Muhammad: 11]? It is said: the "mawla" there means the helper, and here it means the owner. ﴿And what they used to invent﴾ in the world of lies ﴿has vanished from them﴾, that is, it departed from them and became void.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 10, verses 35–36:

﴿Say: Is there any of your partners who guides to the truth?﴾ That is, who gives guidance (yurshidu) ﴿to the truth﴾. So if they say, "No," and they must say that, ﴿Say: God guides to the truth﴾, that is, to the truth.

﴿Is then He who guides to the truth more worthy to be followed, or he who does not find guidance unless he is guided?﴾ Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read yahiddi with a sukun on the ha' and a light dal (ya-hdi). The others read it with a shadda on the dal (yahiddi, from yahtadi, with the ta' assimilated into the dal). Then Abu Ja'far and Qalun read it with a sukun on the ha'; Abu 'Amr read it with rawm on the ha' (a vowel pronounced between fatha and sukun); Hafs read it with a fatha on the ya' and a kasra on the ha'; Abu Bakr read it with a kasra on both; and the rest read it with a fatha on both. Its meaning in all of these readings is "he who finds guidance" (yahtadi). Whoever lightens the dal says: it is said "hadaytuhu, fahuwa yuhda," meaning "ihtada" (he was guided). Whoever shaddes the dal assimilates the ta' into the dal. Then Abu 'Amr uses rawm according to his method of preferring lightening. Whoever makes the ha' sukun leaves it in its state, as he did in "ta'uddu" and "yakhissimun." Whoever makes the ha' fatha transfers the fatha of the assimilated ta' onto the ha'. Whoever makes the ha' kasra does so because of the meeting of two sakins; and it is said that the jazm is moved to kasra. Whoever makes the ya' kasra along with the ha' makes the kasra follow the kasra.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Unless he is guided﴾. The meaning of the verse: Is He who guides to the truth more worthy of being followed, or the idol which does not find guidance unless it is guided?

If it is asked: how does He say "unless it is guided," when it is not conceivable that an idol could find guidance or be guided?

It is said: the meaning of guidance with regard to idols is movement; that is, they do not move from one place to another unless they are carried and transported, which shows the helplessness of the idols.

Another answer is that the mention of guidance is in a figurative sense. That is because when the polytheists took the idols as gods and placed them in the station of one who hears and understands, He expressed them with what is used for one who knows and understands, and they were described with the attribute of one who understands.

﴿What is the matter with you? How do you judge?﴾ How do you decide, when you claim that God has a partner?

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And most of them follow nothing but conjecture﴾ from them. They say that the idols are gods and that they will intercede for them in the Hereafter, out of conjecture on their part, for which no Book and no Messenger has come. By "most" he means all who say that. ﴿Surely conjecture avails nothing against the truth﴾, that is, it does not ward off from them anything of God's punishment. It is also said: it does not stand in the place of knowledge. ﴿Surely God is Knowing of what they do.﴾

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 10, verses 37–41:**

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿It is not [possible] that this Qur'an be fabricated apart from Allah.﴾ Al-Farra' said: its meaning is: "It is not fitting for the likes of this Qur'an to be fabricated apart from Allah," like His saying, the Exalted: ﴿It is not for a Prophet to defraud [his people]﴾ [Al 'Imran: 161].

It was also said: "أَنْ" (an) carries the meaning of "اللَّامِ" (al-lam, "li," meaning "in order that/for"), i.e., "This Qur'an was not [such] that it should be fabricated apart from Allah."

His saying: ﴿But [it is] a confirmation of what was before it﴾ means: of what was before the Qur'an, from the Torah and the Gospel.

It was also said: the confirmation of what was before the Qur'an is [that it confirms] the Resurrection and the raising [of the dead]. ﴿And a detailed explanation of the Book﴾ means: a clarification of what is in the Book of lawful and unlawful, obligations and rulings. ﴿There is no doubt in it, [it is] from the Lord of the worlds.﴾

﴿Or do they say﴾: Abu 'Ubaydah said: "أَمْ" (am) carries the meaning of "الْوَاوِ" (al-waw, "and"), i.e., "And they say." ﴿He has invented it﴾: Muhammad fabricated the Qur'an from his own self. ﴿Say: Then bring a surah like it﴾: similar to the Qur'an. ﴿And call upon whomever you can﴾ from among those you worship, ﴿other than Allah﴾, to help you in that, ﴿if you are truthful﴾ that Muhammad fabricated it. Then He said:

﴿Rather, they have denied that which they did not encompass in knowledge﴾: meaning the Qur'an. They denied it without encompassing its knowledge. ﴿And its interpretation has not yet come to them﴾: i.e., the outcome of what Allah promised in the Qur'an, that their affair would culminate in punishment. He means: they did not know what the outcome of their affair would be.

﴿Thus did those before them deny﴾: i.e., just as these disbelievers denied the Qur'an, so too did those before them, the disbelievers of the earlier nations, deny [their messengers]. ﴿So see how was the end of the wrongdoers﴾: the final fate of the polytheists was destruction.

﴿And among them are those who believe in it﴾: i.e., among your people are those who believe in the Qur'an. ﴿And among them are those who do not believe in it﴾, due to Allah's prior knowledge concerning them. ﴿And your Lord is most knowing of the corrupters﴾ [170/a] who do not believe.

﴿And if they deny you﴾, O Muhammad, ﴿then say: "For me is my deed"﴾ and its recompense, ﴿and for you is your deed﴾ and its recompense. ﴿You are free from what I do, and I am free from what you do.﴾ This is like His saying, the Exalted: ﴿For us are our deeds and for you are your deeds﴾ [al-Qasas: 55], and ﴿For you is your religion, and for me is my religion﴾ [al-Kafirun: 6].

The commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 10, verses 46–50:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Whether We show you (O Muhammad) some of what We threaten them with during your lifetime, or We take you back (in death) before their punishment, to Us is their return in the Hereafter. Then Allah is Witness over what they do﴾, meaning He will recompense them for it. "Thumma" (then) here carries the sense of "wa" (and), so the meaning is: "and Allah is Witness." Mujahid said: The part that He showed him was their killing at Badr, and the rest of the various kinds of punishment came after their death.

The words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿For every nation there is a messenger. When their messenger comes﴾ and they deny him, ﴿judgment is passed between them with justice﴾, meaning they were punished in this world and destroyed by the punishment, that is, before the coming of the messenger, with neither reward nor punishment. Mujahid and Muqatil said: When their messenger who was sent to them comes on the Day of Resurrection, judgment is passed between him and them with justice. ﴿And they are not wronged﴾, meaning they are not punished without sin, nor held to account without proof, nor is any of their good deeds diminished, nor is anything added to their evil deeds.

﴿And they say﴾, that is, the polytheists say: ﴿When is this promise﴾ which you threaten us with, O Muhammad, of punishment? It was said: It refers to the establishment of the Hour. ﴿If you are truthful﴾, you and your followers.

﴿Say: I have no power over my own benefit or harm﴾, meaning I have no ability over either of them to achieve anything, ﴿except what Allah wills﴾ that I should have power over. ﴿For every nation there is a term﴾, an appointed period. ﴿When their term comes﴾, the time of the end of their lives, ﴿they cannot delay it by an hour, nor can they advance it﴾, that is, they cannot postpone it or bring it forward.

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Say: Tell me, if His punishment comes upon you by night﴾, meaning in the night, ﴿or by day, what is it that the criminals seek to hasten?﴾ That is, what is it that the polytheists seek to hasten from Allah? It was also said: What is it that the criminals seek to hasten of the punishment, when they have already fallen into it? The real meaning is that they used to seek the punishment hastily, saying: "O Allah, if this is the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky, or bring us a painful punishment" [al-Anfal: 32]. Then Allah the Exalted says: ﴿What is it that they seek to hasten?﴾, meaning: "ayshin" [[i.e., what?]], the criminals do not know what they are seeking and asking for. It is like a man who says to another, after he has done something foul: "What have you brought upon yourself?"

The commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 10, verses 57–59:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿O mankind, there has certainly come to you an admonition⦆ — a reminder — ﴿from your Lord and a healing for what is in the breasts﴾, that is, a remedy for ignorance, for what is in the breasts. That is, a cure for the blindness of the hearts. The ṣadr (breast) is the place of the heart, and it is the most honoured place in a person because of its proximity to the heart. ﴿And guidance﴾ from misguidance, ﴿and mercy for the believers﴾. Mercy (raḥmah) is a blessing bestowed upon one who is in need. For if a king sends a gift to another king, it is not said that he has shown him mercy, even though it is a blessing, because he has not placed it with one in need.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Say: By the bounty of Allah and by His mercy﴾. Mujahid and Qatadah said: the bounty of Allah is faith, and His mercy is the Qur'an [[See: al-Tabari: 15/107.]]. Abu Sa'id al-Khudri said: the bounty of Allah is the Qur'an, and His mercy is that He made us among its people [[al-Tabari: 15/106. See also al-Durr al-Manthur: 4/367–368, where the remaining opinions are found.]].

Ibn Umar said: the bounty of Allah is Islam, and His mercy is its beautification in the heart.

Khalid ibn Ma'dan said: the bounty of Allah is Islam, and His mercy is the sunan (the prophetic practices and ways).

It has also been said: the bounty of Allah is faith, and His mercy is Paradise.

﴿So let them rejoice﴾, that is, let the believers rejoice that Allah has made them among its people, ﴿it is better than what they accumulate﴾, that is, than the wealth that the disbelievers accumulate. It has also been said that both expressions refer to the disbelievers.

Abu Ja'far and Ibn 'Amir read فَلْيَفْرَحُوا (falyafrahū, "so let them rejoice") with the yā' (the third person plural imperative prefix), and تَجْمَعُونَ (tajma'ūna, "you accumulate") with the tā' (the second person form). Ya'qub read both with the tā', with a variant reported from him, addressing the believers.

﴿Say﴾, O Muhammad, to the disbelievers of Makkah: ﴿Have you considered what Allah has sent down to you of provision﴾. He expressed creation by the term "sending down," because whatever good there is on the earth is, in that sense, sent down by Allah, such as provision of crops and livestock. ﴿And you have made from it lawful and unlawful﴾. This refers to what they forbade of the tilth and of the livestock, such as the baḥīrah (a she-camel whose ear was slit and was left unridden), the sā'ibah (a free-roaming animal), the waṣīlah (a ewe that bore twin females, or a similar animal dedicated to idols), and the ḥām (a stallion camel released after a certain number of covers). Al-Dahhak said: it is His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And they assign to Allah a share of what He has produced of tilth and livestock﴾ [al-An'am: 136] [170/b].

﴿Say: Has Allah permitted you﴾ in this prohibition and permission, ﴿or upon Allah do you invent falsehood?﴾ — here أَمْ (am) means "rather." This is their saying: "Allah has commanded us to do this."

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Upon those who say, "Our Lord is Allah," then remain steadfast, the angels descend upon them, [saying], "Do not fear and do not grieve, but receive good news of Paradise, which you were promised."﴾ [Fussilat: 30]

ʿAtaʾ narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas: "The good news in this world" means: at the time of death, the angels come to them with glad tidings; and in the Hereafter, at the departure of the soul of the believer, it is raised up to Allah and is given good news of Allah's good pleasure.

Al-Hasan said: it is what Allah has given good news to the believers of in His Book, of His Garden and His generous reward, as in His saying: ﴿And give good news to those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾ [al-Baqarah: 25], ﴿and give good news to the believers﴾ [al-Ahzab: 47], and ﴿rejoice in Paradise﴾ [Fussilat: 30].

It is also said: He gave them good news in this world through the Book and the Messenger that they are the friends of Allah, and He gives them good news in the graves and in the books of their deeds of Paradise. [Imam al-Tabari, may Allah have mercy on him, cited the opinions on the meaning of "al-bushra" with which Allah gave good news to these people, then said: "The most correct interpretation of that is that Allah the Exalted informed that His righteous friends have good news in the life of this world. Among the glad tidings in this world is the good dream that a Muslim sees or that is seen for him; among them is the good news of the angels to him at the departure of his soul, with the mercy of Allah, as narrated from the Prophet ﷺ ...; among them is Allah's good news to him of what He promised in His Book and on the tongue of His Messenger ﷺ of abundant reward ... All these meanings are from Allah's good news to him in the life of this world; He gave him good news of them, and Allah did not specify one meaning over another, so it is included in His saying: that for them is good news in the life of this world. As for the Hereafter, it is Paradise." See: Tafsir al-Tabari: 15/140–141.]

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 10, verses 70–72:**

﴿A brief enjoyment﴾ they enjoy in it, and a provision by which they benefit until the end of their terms. And "*matā'un*" (enjoyment) is in the nominative case by an implied subject, meaning: it is an enjoyment ﴿in the world. Then to Us is their return. Then We shall make them taste the severe punishment because they used to disbelieve﴾.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And recite to them the news of Nuh﴾, meaning: recite, O Muhammad, to the people of Makkah the story of Nuh (Noah) ﴿when he said to his people﴾, and they were the descendants of Qabil (Cain), ﴿O my people, if my standing [among you] and my reminding you of the signs of Allah has been burdensome to you﴾, meaning: has been great and heavy upon you, ﴿my standing﴾, meaning the length of my stay among you, ﴿and my reminding﴾ and my admonishing you ﴿of the signs of Allah﴾, by His proofs and clear evidences, so you resolved to kill me and drive me out. ﴿Then upon Allah I have relied. So resolve upon your decision﴾, meaning: make your affair firm and determine upon it, ﴿and [gather] your partners﴾, meaning: call upon your partners, that is, your gods, and seek their help so that they may join with you.

Al-Zajjaj said: Its meaning is: "Resolve your affair together with your partners." When the word "*ma'a*" (with) is omitted, the noun becomes accusative. Ya'qub (a Qur'an reciter) read "*wa-shurakā'ukum*" in the nominative, meaning: resolve your affair, you and your partners together.

﴿Then let not your affair be in confusion for you﴾, meaning: obscure and ambiguous, from their saying: "The crescent was *ghumma* over the people," meaning it was unclear to them. ﴿Then carry out your plan against me﴾, meaning: execute what is in your minds and finish with it. It is said: "So-and-so *qaḍā*," meaning he died and passed away; and "He *qaḍā* his debt," meaning he finished paying it.

It was also said: its meaning is: "Come at me with killing and harm."

It was also said: "Then decide what you are deciding," and this is like the words of the magicians to Pharaoh: ﴿So decide what you are deciding﴾ [Ta-Ha: 72], meaning: do what you are doing.

﴿And do not give me respite﴾, meaning: do not delay. This is in the manner of *ta'jiz* (a challenge to show their helplessness). Allah informed about Nuh that he was confident in the victory of Allah the Exalted and was not afraid of the plotting of his people, knowing that they and their gods had no power to benefit or harm, except as Allah wills.

﴿But if you turn away﴾, meaning: you turn away from my words and refuse my advice, ﴿then I have not asked you﴾ for anything in exchange for conveying the message and the call, ﴿for any reward﴾, meaning recompense or compensation. ﴿My reward is not but from Allah, and I have been commanded to be among the Muslims﴾, meaning: among the believers. It was also said: among those who submit to the command of Allah.

﴿And We drowned those who denied Our signs. So see how was the end of those who were warned﴾, i.e., the final fate of those whom the messengers warned, but who did not believe.

﴿Then after him We sent messengers﴾, i.e., after Nuh, messengers

﴿to their peoples, and they came to them with clear proofs﴾, with manifest evidences. ﴿But they were not going to believe in what they had denied before﴾, i.e., in what the people of Nuh had denied before. ﴿Thus do We seal﴾, i.e., We set a seal, ﴿upon the hearts of the transgressors﴾.

﴿Then after them We sent Musa and Harun to Fir'awn and his chiefs﴾, meaning the nobles of his people, ﴿with Our signs, but they were arrogant, and they were a criminal people﴾.

His saying: ﴿Our Lord, obliterate their wealth﴾. Mujahid said: destroy it. And al-tams (obliteration) is annihilation. Most of the people of tafsir said: transform it and change it from its form.

Qatadah said: their wealth, their crops, their fields and their jewels became stones.

Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: He made their sugar into stones [[See: al-Tabari: 15/179–182; al-Durr al-Manthur: 4/384.]]. A man was with his wife on his bed and they both became two stones, and the woman was standing kneading dough and she became a stone.

Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, said: It has reached us that the dirhams and the dinars became stones, engraved in their former shape, whole, halves and thirds.

'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz called for a small bag containing some remnants of the family of Pharaoh, and he took out from it an egg split in two and a walnut split in two, and indeed it was stone.

As-Suddi said: Allah transformed their wealth into stones, and the palm trees, the fruits, the flour and the foods, and it was one of the nine signs.

﴿And harden their hearts﴾, that is: seal them and set a seal upon them so that they do not soften and do not open up to faith, ﴿so that they will not believe﴾. It was said: it is a subjunctive (nasb) answered by the fa' after the supplication. It was said: it is a conjunction upon His saying "that they may mislead", meaning: that they may mislead, so that they do not believe. Al-Farra' said: it is a supplication whose position is jussive (jazm), as if he said: "O Allah, so that they do not believe." ﴿Until they see the painful punishment﴾, which is drowning. As-Suddi said: its meaning is: cause them to die upon disbelief.

﴿He said﴾: Allah the Exalted said to Moses and Aaron: ﴿Your supplication has been answered﴾. It is attributed to both of them, though the supplication was from Moses, because it is narrated that Moses would supplicate while Aaron said "Amin," and the amin is a supplication. In some narratives: between the supplication of Moses and its answer there were forty years [[See: al-Tabari: 15/187.]].

﴿So remain steadfast﴾ upon the message and the call, and proceed according to My command until the punishment comes to them. ﴿And never follow﴾ is a prohibition with the heavy nun (nun al-thaqilah), and its position is jussive. It is said in the singular: la tattabi'anna with a fatha on the nun, due to the meeting of two unvocalized letters (iltiqa' al-sakinayn); and in the dual, with a kasra on the nun for this same reason. Ibn 'Amir recited with a light nun, because the nun of emphasis (nun al-ta'kid) is both heavy and light. ﴿The path of those who do not know﴾, meaning: do not take the way of those who are ignorant of the reality of My promise, for My promise has no failure in it, and My threat descends upon Pharaoh and his people.

﴿So this day We will save you⁠﴾ i.e., We will cast you upon a elevated place of the earth (najwah), which is a high place. Ya'qub read "nunjika" with the light (takhfif) form. ﴿in your body﴾ with your body, having no spirit in it. It is also said: "in your body" means "in your armour," for he had a famous coat of mail set with jewels, and they saw him in his armour and believed.

﴿so that he may be a sign for those who come after you﴾ a lesson and an admonition. ﴿Indeed, many of the people are heedless of Our signs﴾.

﴿And We certainly settled the Children of Israel﴾ [We caused the Children of Israel to dwell] [[Omitted from "A".]] after the destruction of Pharaoh, ﴿in a good place﴾ a place of truthfulness (manzil sidq), meaning: Egypt. It is also said: the Jordan and Palestine, which is the Holy Land that Allah prescribed as an inheritance [[Addition from "B".]] for Abraham and his offspring. Ad-Dahhak said: it is Egypt and Syria. ﴿And We provided them with good things﴾ the lawful things. ﴿So they did not differ﴾ meaning the Jews who were in the time of the Prophet ﷺ, concerning his truthfulness and that he is a prophet, ﴿until knowledge came to them﴾ meaning: the Qur'an and the clear evidence that he is a truthful messenger [of Allah] [[Addition from "B".]], and that his religion is true.

It is also said: "until there came to them what they knew" (ma'lumuhum), namely Muhammad ﷺ, because they used to know him before his coming out; so "knowledge" here means "the known," just as a created thing is called "khalq" (creation). He said: "Who are you, boy?" He said: "From the people of Yunus." He said: "When you return to them, inform them that I met Yunus." The boy said: "You know that if I have no proof, I will be killed." Yunus, peace be upon him, said: "This plot of ground and this tree will bear witness for you." The boy said: "Then command them." Yunus said: "When this boy comes to you, bear witness for him." They said: "Yes." The boy returned and told the king: "I met Yunus," and the king ordered his execution. He said: "I have proof; send with me." He went to the plot of ground and the tree and said: "I adjure you by Allah, did Yunus call you to witness?" They said: "Yes." The people returned in alarm and said to the king: "The tree and the earth have borne witness for him." His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And if your Lord had willed, those on the earth would have believed, all of them entirely. ﴿And He places the abomination (rijs)﴾ Abu Bakr recited "wa-najʿalu" with the nun, while the rest recited it with the ya', meaning: and Allah places the abomination, i.e., the punishment, which is the rijz, ﴿upon those who do not reason﴾ regarding Allah's command and His prohibition.

﴿Say, "Look"﴾ i.e., say to the polytheists who ask you for signs: look. ﴿at what is in the heavens and the earth﴾ of signs, proofs and lessons. Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 10, verse 102–105:

﴿So are they waiting for anything but like the days of those who passed away before them?﴾ That is, the Meccan polytheists. "Days" (ayyam) means the times that passed, namely the days of those nations who denied their messengers. Qatadah said: it means the events of God against the people of Noah, 'Ad and Thamud. The Arabs call punishment "days" and blessings "days," as in His saying: ﴿And remind them of the Days of God﴾ [Ibrahim: 5]. Everything that has passed over you of good or evil is called "days." ﴿Say: Then wait; indeed I am with you among those who wait.﴾

Ya'qub read "nunji" with a light (takhfif) pronunciation, which is reported differently from him. ﴿And those who believe﴾ along with them at the descent of the punishment. Najja (najja) and anja (anja) have one meaning.

﴿And do not be among the polytheists.﴾

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 10, verses 106–109:**

﴿And do not invoke﴾, meaning, do not worship, ﴿besides Allah that which can neither benefit you﴾ if you obey it, ﴿nor harm you﴾ if you disobey it. ﴿And if you do so﴾, that is, if you worship other than Allah, ﴿then indeed you would be, at that time, among the wrongdoers﴾, those who harm themselves and who place worship in other than its rightful place.

﴿And if Allah touches you with adversity﴾, meaning, afflicts you with hardship and trial, ﴿there is no remover of it﴾, meaning, no one who can repel it, ﴿except Him. And if He intends for you good﴾, meaning, ease, blessing and abundance, ﴿there is no repeller of His bounty﴾, meaning, no one who can withhold His provision. ﴿He causes it to reach whom He wills of His servants﴾, meaning, with each of harm and good, ﴿and He is the Forgiving, the Merciful﴾.

﴿Say, "O mankind, the truth has come to you from your Lord﴾, meaning, the Qur'an and Islam. ﴿So whoever is guided, it is only for [the benefit of] himself that he is guided, and whoever goes astray, it is only against himself that he goes astray﴾, meaning, against his own soul, and its consequence falls upon him. ﴿And I am not over you a guardian﴾, meaning, a custodian, who protects your deeds." Ibn ʿAbbas said: it was abrogated (*naskh*, the cancellation of a ruling by a later revelation) by the verse of fighting.[[See above: 3/32, note (1); al-Fawz al-Kabir by al-Dihlawi, pp. 53, 60.]]

﴿And follow what is revealed to you and be patient until Allah judges﴾, meaning, until He grants you victory, subdues your enemy and makes His religion prevail. ﴿And He is the best of judges﴾. So He judged for fighting against the polytheists and for the *jizyah* (the poll tax) upon the People of the Book, who pay it willingly while they are humbled.
